analysis.title: Rates Spark: Higher rates amid a fragile calm
key_insights: ING returns to a tactically bearish call on global rates after the 2yr USD swap rose about 12bp in a day with no strong catalyst. Higher oil and robust jobless numbers do not explain a move that size.
Risk sentiment is improving as AI worries become more idiosyncratic, centered on questions about NVIDIA's leadership. Equity markets keep buying dips.

Next week brings two AI bellwether events: Anthropic's IPO pricing and NVIDIA's third-quarter results. ING says either could shake the US macro outlook, and recent disappointments have pushed US rates lower quickly.

Europe is relatively shielded from AI risk, but global risk sentiment can pull longer rates down. ING expects the front end of the EUR and GBP curves to stay focused on inflation, with the belly more exposed to sentiment.

The euro swap curve prices an ECB terminal rate above 3%. ING says this holds only if the growth outlook improves materially, and a global AI setback would raise expectations for rate cuts after the initial hiking cycle.

European government bonds are drifting with global sentiment, driven by tech equity jitters, geopolitical unease after comments from US President Trump, and the repricing of rates higher that started in the US.

France lags peers, with the 10y OAT/Bund spread back near 150bp. First polls showed Christine Lagarde at 14% of first-round votes, similar to other centrist candidates. Marine Le Pen and Jean-Luc Mélenchon would advance to the second round, which leaves a tail-risk scenario open.

S&P reviews Italy, currently BBB+ with a positive outlook held since January. An upgrade to single-A is possible, but ING says a postponement would not be a surprise given the more uncertain political and fiscal outlook.

Friday events: ECB speakers including Isabel Schnabel, final October inflation for France and Spain, second reading of Q3 eurozone GDP, US October PPI, and Fed speakers Susan Collins, Lorie Logan and Michelle Bowman. After the close, rating reviews cover Italy (S&P), Germany (Fitch, AAA/Stable), and Portugal and the UK (DBRS).
earnings_insights: NVIDIA is due to announce third-quarter results next week. ING treats it as a bellwether for the future of AI. The report gives no estimates.

trade_ideas.description: Tactically bearish on global rates, meaning higher rates, mainly USD and EUR
trade_ideas.rationale: Price action shows global rates pushing higher again, and risk sentiment is improving as AI worries turn idiosyncratic.
trade_ideas.risk: AI event risk next week (Anthropic IPO pricing, NVIDIA Q3 results) could quickly reverse the move and push rates lower.
